subject: Cloud Computing
title: Reserved Instances and Commitments
description: Learn Reserved Instances and Commitments in one minute.

hook.text: AWS offers a deal: commit to one year and save 40%. Commit to three years and save 60%. Tempting.

buildup.text: Reserved instances trade flexibility for savings. You promise to use a specific amount, and the price drops.

discovery.text: All major clouds offer this: AWS Reserved Instances, Azure Reservations, GCP Committed Use Discounts.

twist.text: Commit to the wrong size or region and you're stuck paying for resources you don't need for years.

climax.text: Reservations save large companies millions per year. But they require accurate forecasting — a rare skill.

punchline.text: Commit and save big. Guess wrong and waste big.

quiz.question: What is the trade-off of reserved instances?
options: Lower prices in exchange for a commitment to use specific resources over time
Higher prices in exchange for more technical support
Free resources in exchange for sharing your data publicly

details.summary: Reserved instances and committed-use discounts offer 30 to 72 percent savings in exchange for committing to one or three years of usage. AWS, Azure, and GCP all offer commitment-based pricing. The savings are substantial but require accurate capacity forecasting.
details.whyItMatters: Reserved instances are the single largest cost optimization lever in cloud. Organizations that run steady workloads on pay-as-you-go pricing are dramatically overspending.
takeaways: Savings of 30 to 72 percent over on-demand pricing
Requires committing to one or three years of usage
Accurate capacity forecasting is essential to avoid waste

faq.question: What happens if you don't use your reserved capacity?
faq.answer: You pay for it anyway. Unused reserved capacity is wasted money. Some providers allow selling unused reservations on a marketplace. AWS Savings Plans offer more flexibility by applying to any instance family within a region.

faq.question: How much should you reserve vs keep on-demand?
faq.answer: Reserve your steady-state baseline load that runs 24/7 and use on-demand or spot for variable and burst capacity. A common starting point is reserving 60 to 70 percent of compute and keeping 30 to 40 percent flexible.
